t:
(a) 
The Trade Agreements Act of 1979 (Public Law 96–39; 93 Stat. 144 et seq.) is amended as follows:

        (1) 
Section 852 is amended by striking out:

“So much of subpart D of part 12 of schedule 1 of the Tariff Schedules of the United States as follows headnote 1 is amended to read as follows:




 
“
 
Aquavit
 

 
”
 



and inserting in lieu thereof the following:

“Subpart D of part 12 of schedule 1 of the Tariff Schedules of the United States is amended to read as follows:




 
“
 
Subpart D headnote:  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
1. The rates of duty provided for the products enumerated in this subpart shall be assessed on a proof gallon basis (i.e., the rates shown indicate the amount of duty which shall be collected on each gallon of an imported product at 100 proof). The amount of duty which shall be collected for each gallon of a product which is imported at more than or less than 100 proof shall bear the same ratio to the applicable rate of duty as the proof of the imported product bears to 100 proof.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Aquavit:
 
 
 
”
 




 
        (2) 
Paragraph (1) of section 1107(a) is amended to read as follows:


“(1) 
by inserting ‘and’ after ‘subpart E,’, and by striking out ‘headnote 4’ and inserting in lieu thereof ‘headnote 3’, in headnote 3(a)(i), and”.



 
        (3) 
The amendments made by this subsection shall apply with respect to articles entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or after January 1, 1980.
  
    (b) 
The amendments made to the Trade Agreements Act of 1979 by section 14(a)(3)(A) of Public Law 96–467 with respect to items 678.50, 694.15, 694.20, and 694.40 of the Tariff schedules of the United States shall apply with respect to articles entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or after January 1, 1980.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to tariff schedule headnotes on proof-gallon duty rates and sets effective dates for articles entered or withdrawn from warehouse. The tempting reading is that "Trade Agreements Act" implies negotiation or agreement with outside parties, but the word appears only in a proper noun. No consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government is created.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to tariff schedules and duty rates under the Trade Agreements Act. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, advisory boards with non-federal members, or rights to sue. The text merely changes the legal text regarding how duties are assessed on imported goods.
qwen_block.s: Section 852 is amended by striking out... and inserting in lieu thereof the following... The amendments made by this subsection shall apply with respect to articles entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption on or after January 1, 1980.

opus.w: This section only makes technical amendments to tariff schedule language (how duty rates on aquavit and other spirits are assessed) and sets effective dates for entries on or after January 1, 1980. Nothing in it brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision: there is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue. The word "Agreements" in the Act's title is boilerplate and does not create any participation process.
opus.b: This is a technical tariff amendment. It changes how duties on aquavit and other spirits are calculated (on a proof-gallon basis), fixes headnote cross-references, and sets effective dates. A reader might be drawn in by the name "Trade Agreements Act," but the word "Agreements" is just part of the title. The section sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue, so nobody outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Trade Agreements Act to change tariff schedules and headnotes. It specifies the new text for tariff classifications and the effective date for these changes. There is no requirement for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or any other form of participation by non-federal parties in the decision-making process described here. The changes are enacted directly by legislative amendment.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing tariff schedules affects the public or companies, so it involves participation. However, the text itself only describes legislative amendments to tariff codes and effective dates. It does not mandate any process for consulting with the public, states, or other outside entities before making these changes. The changes are made by Congress via statute, not through a participatory process described in this section.
